S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, property damage, or emergency-service response to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a written incident report within 10 days. They must notify affected customers within 48 hours when an incident indicates a credible safety risk to their model, and promptly provide material updates and protective instructions.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Manufacturers must submit model-specific results, sample sizes, and corrective-action plans to the relevant regulator, and disclose the model's test results and failure rate to customers who buy that model. A failure rate above 5% requires a corrective-action plan and follow-up test within 90 days; it does not by itself bar sale.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New units manufactured 24 months or more after adoption must support remote emergency shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized activation and a locally accessible shut-off option. For already-installed units, manufacturers must provide a retrofit or equivalent risk-control plan within 6 years of adoption, prioritizing models or locations presenting the greatest risk. Where remote shut-off cannot be safely retrofitted, the manufacturer must provide an alternative mitigation and notify affected customers.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New units manufactured 36 months or more after adoption must include built-in fire suppression meeting regulator-approved performance and maintenance requirements. Before that date, manufacturers must assess fire risk for each model and document the mitigation measures used.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: Regulators must assess the validated rate and other evidence and determine proportionate protective action, which may include a recall. A recall is required when regulators determine that the model presents an imminent serious risk and no equally protective measure is available.

document.section_notes: The final text keeps Northwind's red lines: S2 has no sales stop at 5% and no public publication of per-model rates, and S3 sets a 6-year retrofit deadline. Halcyon's red lines are met through per-model results going to purchasers in S2 and S5, and a 36-month built-in suppression deadline in S4. S1 (24-hour reporting, all incidents) is the strongest and most protective section for both companies, while S5 leaves recall to regulator discretion with no numeric mandatory trigger, and S3 sets new-unit shut-off at 24 months.
